GDG-USAR Student Handbook
 Sample source document for Task 3: AI-Powered Document Assistant
About This Document
This fictional handbook is provided for the AI-Powered Document Assistant project. It contains sample
information about student support, club activities, event participation, and project submissions. It is not an official
university policy document. Students should build their assistant so that answers are grounded in the text below
and unsupported questions are clearly identified.

1. Student Support Desk
The Student Support Desk helps students find the correct university office for common academic and campus
questions. The desk is open Monday to Friday, from 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM. It is closed on weekends and
declared university holidays.
Students can contact the desk by email at support@example.edu or visit Room 204, Student Services Building.
The desk can guide students on whe

support@example.edu or visit Room 204, Student Services Building.
The desk can guide students on where to submit a request, but it does not approve academic extensions, fee
refunds, or attendance exemptions.
For course registration questions, students should contact the academic office. For fee payment issues, they
should contact the accounts office. For technical problems with the learning portal, they should contact the IT
help desk.

2. GDG On Campus USAR
GDG On Campus USAR is a student community focused on learning, building projects, and sharing technical
knowledge. Its activities may include workshops, study sessions, project showcases, and talks by invited
speakers.
Students from any year or department may attend open community events, subject to venue capacity and
event-specific registration requirements. Some activities may have limited seats. If registration is required, the
eve

event announcement will include the registration process and deadline.
The community currently organizes learning activities across four broad areas: Development, Machine Learning,
Data Structures and Algorithms, and Cybersecurity. Non-technical activities may also be organized to support
communication, collaboration, and community participation.

3. Workshop Participation
A typical technical workshop includes a short introduction, a guided hands-on activity, and time for questions.
Participants should bring a laptop when the event announcement says that a laptop is required. If a workshop
uses an online tool or repository, the organizer should share the relevant links before the session.
Participants are encouraged to install required software in advance. If installation is not possible, they

ipants are encouraged to install required software in advance. If installation is not possible, they should
inform the organizers before the workshop. Organizers may provide an alternative such as a browser-based
environment, but this is not guaranteed for every event.
Attendance at a workshop does not automatically provide a certificate. If a certificate is offered, its eligibility
conditions will be stated in the event announcement.

4. Project Submissions
For community project activities, teams should submit their work using the platform and format specified in the
task announcement. Unless a task says otherwise, a GitHub repository is recommended for code-based
projects.
A project repository should include a README that explains the project goal, setup instructions, how to run the
project, and any important limitations. Teams should also include a DECISIONS.md file describing at least one
meaningful technical or design dec

s should also include a DECISIONS.md file describing at least one
meaningful technical or design decision, including an alternative considered and the reason for the final choice.
If AI tools are used, teams should document their use in AI_USAGE.md. This file should briefly state which tools
were used, what they were used for, and what parts of the work were reviewed or modified by the team.
Students remain responsible for understanding and explaining their submissions.

Can students from other departments attend open events?

Does the Student Support Desk approve attendance exemptions?
No. The desk can guide students to the appropriate office but does not approve attendance exemptions.
